name: John Gould
role: Messenger to Missouri in 1833 and later Seventy president
dateNote: He was baptized on 16 December 1832 and went to Missouri with Orson Hyde in August 1833.
importance: In August 1833 he and Orson Hyde carried Joseph Smith’s instructions to the Church leaders in Missouri. Section 100 assures Joseph that the two are “in my hands”. They returned with news of the Jackson County violence, which stands behind section 101. He later recruited for the Camp of Israel and served as a president of the Seventy in 1837.
connections: Reynolds Cahoon baptized him, and his companion to Missouri was Orson Hyde.

sources.title: John Gould, Joseph Smith Papers biography

reviewNote: JSP: born 21 Dec. 1784, New Hampshire; Freewill Baptist minister; baptized by Reynolds Cahoon 16 Dec. 1832; to Missouri with Orson Hyde Aug. 1833; president of the Seventy 6 Apr.–3 Sept. 1837; joined Strang’s church by 1846; died 25 June 1855, Knox County, Illinois.
